message:
Interfaces fit from soil to bin without a gap or a clash. Plain words: the front cuts a narrow slot and leaves side rows where the wide ladder passes, the ladder drops over its top into the hopper mouth, and the hopper screw feeds the rear outlet that lifts over the bin lip while cameras guide the reverse-in. Cut of 11.0 N from the kerf scaling calc (E64) feeds the ladder fill in 112 s to 15.0 kg from the hopper filling simulation (E11), and pivot at 0.550 m clears 0.400 m lip by 0.150 m from the tip dump clearance simulation (E51) with digging end leading and dump end trailing.

Limits close with room to spare and old double values reconciled. Plain words: the machine stows like a suitcase, weighs like a person with a bag spare, pulls far harder than it cuts, sips its pack, flexes only a finger width, and stops in a shoe length. Stowed 0.900 m by 0.420 m by 0.450 m against 1.00 m by 0.500 m by 0.500 m from the dump clearance simulation (E51), mass 46.0 kg against 60.0 kg leaving 14.0 kg from the updated mass sum (E62) and mass checks (E66)(E67), traction 294 N from the tip-over and stopping check (E23) against 11.0 N cut, dig 16.4 W from the ladder power estimate (E59) and 0.512 Wh per trip from the dig energy estimate (E60) against 480 Wh pack, sag 3.96 mm from the stiffened sag estimate (E63) down from 72.9 mm from the cantilever deflection estimate (E43) via twin-tube stiffness (E61), stop 0.0625 m brake-only from the tip-over and stopping check (E23) versus 0.308 m with loss from the link-loss simulation (E32), drift 0.100 m to 0.150 m with 5.00 m reset from the drift simulation (E33).

Opinions are answered but votes on this version are still owed. Plain words: frame bend is fixed by larger twin tubes, power is closed by lamp-bulb digging, tip risk is held by light level-only dumping, and arching plus edge wear plus tag visibility become bench tests not blocks. Tip factor 1.69 level-only with 15.0 kg plus 4.50 kg steel from the dump clearance simulation (E51) replaces 4.67 unraised from the tip-over and stopping check (E23), heating rise 18.0 K from the motor heating estimate (E44) is warm skin, so Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead, Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead, Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead and Power Structure and Integration Lead each owe a vote on version 1.

RECORD: Decided skid wheels (C9) plus kerf loosener (C36) plus ladder lift (C2) plus wedge hopper (C4) plus screw tilt pour (C37) plus camera operation (C16); numbers standing mass 46.0 kg vs 60.0 kg (E62)(E66)(E67), stowed 0.90 by 0.42 by 0.45 m (E51), cut 11.0 N (E64) vs traction 294 N (E23), power 16.4 W (E59) energy 0.512 Wh (E60), sag 3.96 mm (E63), stop 0.0625 vs 0.308 m (E23)(E32), drift 0.10 to 0.15 m (E33), clearance 0.15 m tip 1.69 (E51); open bench tests arching wear fiducial plus votes on version 1 owed by all leads.
Note on Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead: clear kerf plus metered pour that held traction and blind accuracy.
Note on Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead: quantified clearance plus tip that forced light level-only trips.
Note on Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead: bounded stop plus drift plus align that made blind work testable.
Note on Power Structure and Integration Lead: closed mass plus power plus stiffness that fixed the frame.
Not ready, because votes on version 1 and bench tests for arching, wear and tag visibility are still open.
